description.en: The oldest and most visited zoo in Mexico, located within the historic Chapultepec Park in the heart of Mexico City.
The second largest zoo in Mexico City, focused on the conservation of native and endangered species like the Mexican wolf.
One of the most modern zoos in Latin America, spectacularly situated on the edge of the Huentitán Canyon in Jalisco.
A state-of-the-art subterranean aquarium in Polanco, housing thousands of marine creatures across four underground levels.

en: Home to gentoo and chinstrap penguins

description.en: A premier eco-archaeological park on the Riviera Maya that celebrates Mexican culture, history, and natural beauty.

en: Famous for its nightly folklore show

description.en: A renowned wildlife park near Puebla where animals roam freely in large habitats that visitors explore by car or bus.
A massive theme park and safari preserve in the State of Mexico, offering interactive animal encounters and prehistoric exhibits.
A UNESCO World Heritage site in the mountains of Michoacán where millions of monarch butterflies overwinter every year.
A vast biosphere reserve on the Caribbean coast, encompassing tropical forests, mangroves, and pristine coral reefs.

en: Second-largest reef system in the world

description.en: A massive tropical forest reserve in Campeche that protects one of the most powerful ancient Maya cities ever discovered.

en: Largest tropical forest reserve in Mexico
Highest density of jaguars in the country

description.en: One of North America's largest remaining rainforests, home to the Lacandon Maya and an incredible variety of tropical wildlife.

en: Habitat for the rare harpy eagle

description.en: Mexico's largest protected area, famous for its coastal lagoons that serve as the primary calving grounds for gray whales.
A coastal wetland in Yucatán famous for its thousands of pink flamingos and diverse mangrove ecosystems.
A community-managed nature reserve in Oaxaca dedicated to the restoration of mangroves and the protection of sea turtles.
An ecological hotspot in Veracruz where tropical rainforests meet volcanic mountains and the shores of the Gulf of Mexico.

en: Region of the ancient Olmec culture

description.en: A stunningly diverse biosphere reserve in Querétaro, ranging from arid deserts to lush, high-altitude cloud forests.

en: UNESCO site for nature and culture

description.en: A tranquil, car-free island in northern Yucatán known for its sandy streets, vibrant murals, and summer whale shark sightings.

en: No paved roads on the island

description.en: A picturesque Caribbean island near Cancún, famous for the calm, turquoise waters of Playa Norte and its laid-back charm.

en: Temple of goddess Ixchel at Punta Sur

description.en: The most famous island in Lake Pátzcuaro, recognized for its iconic butterfly net fishermen and monumental statue.

en: Statue of Morelos is 40 meters high
Heart of Day of the Dead traditions

description.en: An uninhabited desert island in the Sea of Cortez, celebrated for its red volcanic cliffs and friendly sea lion colony.

en: Home to a permanent sea lion colony

description.en: Mexico's largest island, maintained as a wild and sacred ecological reserve by the indigenous Seri people of Sonora.

en: Ancestral land of the Seri people

description.en: Small volcanic islands off the coast of Nayarit, world-famous for the 'Hidden Beach' nestled inside a collapsed crater.
A strictly protected national park north of Isla Mujeres, serving as the most important nesting site for seabirds in the region.
A UNESCO World Heritage landscape in Jalisco where the blue agave has been cultivated for centuries to produce tequila.
The premier wine region of Mexico, located in Baja California and producing nearly 90% of the country's wine.
Historic coffee-growing estates in the misty highlands of Veracruz, where some of Mexico's finest shade-grown coffee is produced.

en: First place in Mexico to grow coffee
Grown in the Sierra Madre Oriental

description.en: Expansive coffee estates in the rugged mountains of Chiapas, a world leader in organic and fair-trade coffee production.
The traditional heartland of mezcal production in Oaxaca, where diverse agave species are harvested for artisanal spirits.
The world's leading avocado-producing region, with vast orchards stretching across the fertile volcanic hills of Michoacán.

en: Trees can bloom four times a year

description.en: Lush tropical orchards in the coastal plains of Sinaloa, one of Mexico's most productive agricultural and mango-exporting hubs.
